a1_answer:
NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first: A pulsed-flow orthophosphate dosing system to reduce lead release from service lines. Standard practice: Continuous orthophosphate dosing at constant concentration and flow. Mitigation: Pulsed dosing at higher peak concentration with periodic flow interruption to promote stable lead-phosphate mineral scale formation. Adjacent-technique clearance: Closest existing practice is continuous corrosion inhibitor dosing; departure is the pulsing schedule which creates supersaturation cycles that accelerate scale nucleation. Mechanism: The pulsed dosing creates periodic high-concentration conditions that drive precipitation of lead-phosphate minerals (pyromorphite) on the pipe surface, reducing soluble lead release.

PHYSICS CHECK — DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = orthophosphate concentration at pipe surface; the mechanism moves it UP by 3-5× during pulse cycles; this REDUCES lead release by promoting stable mineral formation. Governing relation: Scale formation rate ∝ [PO₄³⁻]²·[Pb²⁺] (supersaturation-driven precipitation). Pulsing creates transient supersaturation (3-5× baseline) that accelerates nucleation, forming a protective scale that reduces lead release by >90% per EPA pilot studies.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (a) Existing dosing pump, (b) Standard solenoid valve (DN25, normally closed), (c) Programmable timer (24-hour cycle, 1-hour pulse every 6 hours). Installation: (a) Dosing pump (existing), (b) Solenoid valve installed on discharge line (as-sold, no pipe modification), (c) Timer wired to pump and solenoid valve control circuit (standard wiring). Operation: Timer activates pump at 100% capacity for 1-hour pulses every 6 hours; solenoid valve opens during pulse to deliver 3× normal dose concentration; system otherwise at standby.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice: Continuous pump operation (24/7), 0.5 L/min flow, 100% operational burden. Intervention: (a) Dosing pump (existing, same burden), (b) Solenoid valve (DN25, catalog part, install burden = standard valve), (c) Timer (programmable, catalog part, install burden = standard controller). Burden parity: Same operational maintenance (no additional consumables), same energy use (pump runs 4 hours/day vs 24, but at 100% capacity), same installation complexity (one valve and one timer added, both standard plumbing/electrical work). Operational loss: Zero (pulsing occurs during normal operational windows).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install test loop with lead pipe coupons; measure lead release in stagnant and flowing conditions. Instruments: ICP-MS for lead analysis, flow meter, pressure gauge. Pass/fail: 90th percentile lead concentration <5 ppb after 12-month exposure. Duration: 12-month continuous test with monthly sampling. Kill criterion: Any single sample >15 ppb or 90th percentile >5 ppb at 6-month interim. Falsification: Compare continuous dosing vs pulsed dosing side-by-side; pulsed system must show statistically significant (p<0.05) lead reduction.
